tasks.old_behavior: When --negotiation-restrict receives an unresolvable ref name (not a valid object), git dies with error message "%s is not a valid object".
tasks.new_behavior: When --negotiation-restrict receives an unresolvable ref name, it is silently ignored (continue). Only missing objects that exist as ref targets still die. The error message for glob patterns that match no refs now shows the option name (--negotiation-restrict) instead of being hardcoded.
tasks.compatibility_reason: Scripts or tools that rely on git fetch --negotiation-restrict to fail with a non-zero exit code on invalid ref names will no longer detect the error. This is a silent contract relaxation that could mask user errors or CI misconfiguration.
tasks.test_recommendation: Test that git fetch --negotiation-restrict=invalid-ref no longer exits non-zero, and that it still fails on a valid ref name pointing to a non-existent object.
